newsitem.title: USA: Capital gains tax cut likely, Rubin says.
newsitem.headline: Capital gains tax cut likely, Rubin says.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin reiterated on Monday the Clinton administration's opposition to a broad-based capital gains tax cut, but acknowledged that one was likely.
"We have never been in favor of a broad-based capital gains tax cut," he told reporters. "On the other hand, we've always said that it's likely because Republicans do favor it."
Bill Archer, Chairman of the House Ways and Means Committee, earlier proposed a cut in the capital gains tax to 20 percent from 28 percent as part of a broad tax plan.
The Texas Republican also backed indexation of capital gains for inflation, starting in 2001.
"Indexing is the piece of capital gains that we are most troubled about," Rubin said, in part because of its potential long-term impact on government revenues.
